subject: Brightline SSO/SCIM — implementation cadence & service-account gating
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@brightline.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Brightline SSO/SCIM — kickoff + MAP (v1)

Julie — thanks for the time today. As promised, attaching the initial mutual action plan (brightline-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short checklist for SSO/SCIM/IP gating. High-level asks to unblock our engineers: 

- SAML IdP metadata (metadata URL or XML file) and whether you prefer SP-initiated or IdP-initiated flow.
- Attribute map (email, firstName, lastName, groups) and whether groups are in the assertion or via SCIM only.
- SCIM endpoint, auth method for provisioning (service account credentials or OAuth), and expected provisioning rate (users/min).
- IP allowlist ranges for Brightline admins / test locations and any egress restrictions we need to be aware of.
- Desired service-account naming convention and required scopes (provisioning, read-only, admin).
- Org policy constraints (least privilege windows, test org vs prod org mapping).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You send IdP metadata + SCIM endpoint + test admin contact by EOD Tue 2026-09-29.
2) We provision a Redwood test service account (ephemeral credentials) and run a smoke provisioning with 2 users.
3) Schedule a 60-min integration call (engineer + admin) Wed 2026-09-30 09:30 PT to validate attributes and run the MAP items.

If that cadence works, we can lock the canary cutover for the following week.

Rishi
Head of Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: brightline-MAP-v1.xlsx

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers and attachments below: 

- Attaching our IdP metadata (brightline-idp-metadata.xml). We run Okta; SP-initiated is preferred but we can support IdP-initiated for admins.
- Attribute assertions include email (primary), given_name, family_name, and groups (we send groups in the assertion).
- SCIM: endpoint is https://scim-api.brightline.com/v2/; we currently support Basic auth for service accounts.
- Provisioning rate: roughly 20 users/min for initial sync; peak spikes during org pulls may be higher — we can provide a CSV sample.
- IP ranges: 52.23.160.0/20 and 18.205.0.0/16 (we'll confirm with Security).
- Service account: we prefer a named account per integration; guidance welcome.

We can do Wed 09/30 09:30 PT — Julie + our platform engineer (cc'd once I loop them in).

Julie Park
Director, IT Operations
Brightline

Fantastic, Julie — thanks for the quick info and the metadata. A couple of implementation notes from CS side before the Wed call so we can come prepared: 

- I'll upload the MAP v1 to the shared Drive and add expected owners for each line item (integration owner, security reviewer, QA). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/brightline/onboarding/MAP-v1
- For SCIM mapping: please review the scim-mapping-template.csv (attached) ahead of the call; we'll align attribute keys and group membership semantics.
- Test users: do you have a dedicated test org or test tenant? If not, we typically recommend 2 test accounts in prod with a low-impact group for verification.
- For IP allowlist: if Security provides CIDR blocks, we'll add them to our egress allowlist and confirm connectivity during the call.
- Service-account rotation window: we default to 90 days for provisioning accounts; if you have stricter rotation policies, please flag.

Looking forward to Wednesday — I'll send a calendar invite for 09/30 09:30 PT with the integration agenda.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: scim-mapping-template.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@brightline.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline SSO/SCIM — kickoff + MAP (v1)

Julie — thanks for the metadata and endpoint. A few technical details we'll validate on Wed; calling them out here so your engineer can prepare. 

1) SAML: we expect the following inbound attributes: 
   - email (NameID preferred, format: persistent)
   - given_name, family_name (standard claims)
   - groups (array) — if groups are in assertion we'll reconcile with SCIM-based group sync and prefer groups-from-SCIM for long-term membership reconciles.

2) SCIM auth: Basic auth with a scoped service account works. Please provision a read/write credential with these scopes: Users:rw, Groups:rw, Schema:read. If Brightline prefers OAuth, we can support that but will need client_id/secret ahead of the call.

3) Rate limits & batching: our side expects up to 50 req/s for bulk operations during initial imports; we can throttle to your 20 users/min target but need a short window to run a canary (2k users) to validate mapping.

4) IP allowlist: we'll originate provisioning calls from these Redwood egress IPs: 3.214.45.12, 3.214.45.13, 3.214.45.14. Please add to allowlist for the test window and prod.

5) Service account naming: we suggest brightline-redwood-provisioner@brightline.com and a separate brightline-redwood-webhook@brightline.com for event callbacks. Attach: service-account-guidelines.pdf for recommended least-privilege scopes and rotation.

6) Edge cases: SCIM deprovision vs suspended status mapping (we usually map scim:active=false -> suspend). Please confirm desired behavior.

I'll be on the Wed call (engineer pairing). If Brightline can share a CSV sample of 100 users and a sample group structure, we can pre-run a dry sync on our staging environment.

Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference
